Hi,

Timothée here, CEO of Rusty Crewmate.
I believe there is a lot of discussion about this proposal.

How can we improve the visibility of the community on what has been done during those two months?

Nathan, Ramsey, and I were all present for a big AMA a few weeks ago, and no questions were asked on this subject. Does the community need another AMA to take place in order to explore this specific subject?

> We have a decent tracking scheme its our trello process, personally, i would not subject anyone to anything more than that.

This is all fair enough. I don't need to read more the wall of text below that sentence: I heard some concerns before by various people, and offering some way to cut out any possibility for subsequent ones. If you have trello and you say it's fine, please ignore me, don't change anything and good luck!

> I don't need to read more the wall of text below that sentence.

I have responded to each of your points. I get criticised for not answering questions, so i though i would improve by spending more time answering each of your points. 

> I heard some concerns before by various people, and offering some way to cut out any possibility for subsequent ones. 

I am genuinely grateful for your considerations toward subsequent concerns, thank you. 

Let me refer you back to how the kabocha process is the best public collaborative and accountability approach than anyone else in this community. The granularity and public nature of our Backlog, WIP, and Done tasks on the trello board is setting a precedent for the other contributors to follow suite, to share and collaborate their tasks and processes publicly, if they so wish. It's a great way to stay accountable. 

> If you have trello and you say it's fine, please ignore me, don't change anything and good luck!

Trello is great, i don't wish to ignore you, i hope i didn't come across dismissive. 

We will be improving the kanban ticketing process thats for sure, more linking to github. It's all an improvement. 

The thing about process i know it can be a hardcore subject. Even in agile development, some people are hardcore scrum maxis, and others live by kanban. However we form our own heuristic. We are not going to be able to resolve every concern, because not all concerns are resolvable and not all are genuine, however we will do our best to improve. 

Please make a thread for your views on time management systems and general proposals, i'd be interested to see the discussion there.

On a general note, I am always looking to improve in my performance, i am learning new lessons in life every day. And i hope so tom there will be an improve with the communication, structure, agreements and proposals, from myself and everyone i engage with. 

> But it's not what my post is about.
> What I would like to see is for everyone an 1. U[p]front agreement (does not necessarily means upfront funded, it could be postpaid).

Ok, we can make that more formally written in next propsals, because there was an upfront agreement but the formality is the issue. Maybe we can mint the agreements in future.

> on a list of 2. Owned tasks

In this scenario is was harder to know what the owned tasks were, which is the reason we structured it this way.

> with 3. deadlines (or milestones if the task in question is big and needs to be split to fit into proper tracking assessment scheme.
 
We have a decent tracking scheme its our trello process, personally, i would not subject anyone to anything more than that. 

> 4. Ensure that everyone bills for something different.

There has not been one single instance of "double billing". So theres no issue there. We are also each different people working on things, and sometimes on the same thing, and that is sometimes when the best work happens, we buddy up. So its actually encouraged to support each other. So if there is this type of granularity of who provided what value, then it can affect the collaborative culture. I hope that is reasonable for you to get? It may seem splitting hairs, but this subtlety can have a huge impact on the dynamic and morale of collaboration. 

Please, in future if you have general points like above, do you mind making it a new thread. The key reason is that the people who are getting funded, can feel like they are at the receiving end of the criticism, which they are not. 

@nathan if you are reading just want you to know this is purely related to structure of payment of which there is a shifting one w

> But it's not what my post is about.
> What I would like to see is for everyone an 1. U[p]front agreement (does not necessarily means upfront funded, it could be postpaid).
Ok, we can make that more written in next propsals. It can be more formal at least. Because there was an upfront agreement. Maybe we can mint the agreements.

> on a list of 2. Owned tasks
In this scenario is was harder to know what the owned tasks were, which is the reason we structured it this way.
> with 3. deadlines (or milestones if the task in question is big and needs to be split to fit into proper tracking assessment scheme.) and 
We have a decent tracking scheme its our trello process, personally, i would not subject anyone to anything more than that. 
> 4. Ensure that everyone bills for something different.
There has not been one single instance of "double billing". So theres no issue there. We are also each different people working on things. Sometimes tasks are shared. And actually its encouraged to help others. So if there is this type of granularity of who provided what value, then it can affect the collaborative culture. 

Please, in future if you have general points like above, do you mind making it a new thread. The key reason is that the people who are getting funded, can feel like they are at the receiving end of the criticism, which they are not. 

@nathan if you are reading just want you to know this is purely related to structure of payment of which there is a shifitng one with varied points of view. 


If the funding was based on specific tasks then it would be fixed. You see this all the time with grant proposals, teams that achieve one milestone but might want to pivot on other milestones, but are stuck in relation to the fixed things the funding is earmarked for. This can strangle dynamism. Nonetheless structure needs to be context dependant, and of course its great in many situations. 

This funding structure is not ongoing btw , future work will be made with a separate agreement, where we can assess whats best way to structure. I also have not seen any other monthly payments have that level of itemisation. If anyone wants to see what myself or nathan have done they can look on the trello board of tasks. There you will have a granular breakdown of whats done, in public. I believe we are setting an example here for others. I would really like to see what others are working on, if everyone can make their task process public, it would be useful and it would help others to learn to take on those roles in future. I am not going to ask people individually because i dont want to come across interrogatory. 

There was a two month window to get Kabocha to a certain point. This was not a pallet or specific bounty proposal. That's why we went with a 2 x monthly payment approach, where Nathan was assigned as a full time person working on Kabocha repo. Notably, he helped to make a custom [relay chain pallet](https://trello.com/c/OfawkAZ5), as well as create scripts to debug some quite challenging tasks related to distribution. 

> On the flip side, it's also a viable model to have a single person ask for the full funding in one proposal and deal with getting his resources as required.
I think what you are prescribing here is a way you think it should be, when that is not the way it could have been given Nathan's relationship to Rusty Crewmates at the time. Maybe it can be structured like that in future. But i think a pretty good job was done to structure it and value has been provided to both parties. As a steward thats the best i can do. Though im sure its never really, enough, i'm learning to come to terms with that. 

> ...to have a single person ask for the full funding in one proposal and deal with getting his resources as required.
Thats what this is. Assigning Nathan as a core contributor to the Kabocha repo. Sure we can improve the structure. 

There is no way contributors want to be subjected to this process as it currently stands. Its not something that any needs to or should go through, it creates toxic feelings in peoples body, who are dedicated to their work, but can have a seemingly negative criticisms over pay. If there was a Glassdoor reviews version for web3 contributors, im afraid that Edgeware up till now, would have some pretty shitty reviews, when it comes to this part of the process. 

> to have a single person ask for the full funding
Actually i think that has become off the table for contributors to make their own proposals, which is why a steward is needed,  this is due to the general tonality of the comments, and sea gull shits, related to these proposals, and internal frustrations seeping out. It scares people off. I think some of us are more numbed than others when it comes to the tone of criticism, (and some getting used to it). It can be quite discouraging for the contributors. Also using specific proposal to make a general point is perhaps inappropriate for the place. Also i think some of your comments are directed to me and nothing really to do with payee in question. But it can come across relatively harsh to anyone on the receiving end, who is looking at this proposal, hoping for no negative reviews, in fear that they won't get paid. 

> You can ask the RC folks since I am pretty sure they are already accustomed to work within this model.
I was working with RC on this structure, and it was suitable for assigning one person as full time to support the delivery of Kabocha and work on the repo.

body:
Sure, I  cannot really know about the opinion of others and it seems I am the only one commenting here, but some of the previous proposals were not all well received, so maybe some people indeed would like to have a fully granular structure, and yes, I think it would be overkill.
But it's not what my post is about. 
I did not ask to separate all into separate bounties. 
What I would like to see is for everyone an **1. Ufront agreement** (does not necessarily means upfront funded, it could be postpaid) on a list of **2.** **Owned** tasks
with **3. deadlines** (or milestones if the task in question is big and needs to be split to fit a into proper tracking assessment scheme.) and 4. Ensure that everyone bills for **something different**.

This has nothing to do with the reputation of Rusty Crewmates, and also had nothing to do with productivity, this is about proper assessment of who bills for what and we need to know this upfront obviously. 

As far as I am concerned, you could just copy paste part of your trello in the proposals provided they don't overlap, and it is up to the team to organise as they see fit. 
But it will help myself at least to understand what's exactly done by whom. We will see also if anybody's regularly late, or whether people tend to budget too many or too few man days to some tasks, etc.

Since it seems that I am the only one commenting here, maybe I am the only one with a problem, and then it could safely be ignored, but I would not like to see a situation where people will remove their support brutally because they are served the same arguments about reputation or pettiness: any PM does need a plan to get funding and be ready to defend it.
We see this everywhere, even in the web3 world, and I have not seen so many people approaching this with just "this is too low end for us, we deserve better". That's what my comment is about, no more, no less.

You can ask the RC folks since I am pretty sure they are already accustomed to work within this

You can ask the RC folks since I am pretty sure they are already accustomed to work within this model.

On the flip side, it's also a viable model to have a single person ask for the full funding in one proposal and deal with getting his resources as required. 
But that would still need the justification of tasks, deadlines and man-days for the different resources. So the KAB team should have full latitude in organizing its own operations as they like provided they meet the terms of the contract. That also concentrates the responsibilities for any issue onto a single person so it's a tradeoff.

Since there is no update on that proposal, I just wish to clarify and point out some summary of what we discussed on the matter privately since ideally those discussions should all be public.

At a personal level I totally understand the value of - and am fine with - hiring any developer temporarily or permanently as need be. 
The points that I insisted on - and that was also contentious with other members according to the discussions within July - is that without any set of clear milestones, we are unable to know what we are invoiced for and it brings all kind of discussions and confusions. 

The deliverables above are nothing really helpful in understanding what's required. Instead we should have a list of tasks and timelines, even a high level ones that will be owned by the developer, in the sense that he would be personally responsible for the deliveries and the timeframe. 
This combined to proposals from your side (in advance, since postpayment is possible but contracts are always set in advance) and from other developers, we can ensure there is no overlap. 

Otherwise, developer 1 will deliver something, and then developer 2 will also put this in the list of what he delivered and so forth and nobody will be happy. And when there are 10 developers, it's a total anarchy. There is clearly work to do for everybody, so it just needs to be clear which part belongs to whom in all proposals.

Thanks for this, yes its fair that a monthly payment structure is slightly less defined and slightly more broad than other payment structures. And to be fair we have been structuring, starting with bounties, thereafter some pallet proposals, which were clear have been delivered and in progress. 

We have experimented though with 2 months of monthly payments (for Nathan), because the board of tasks shared below were quite varied, it would beaurocratic issue to have to create bounty for each tasks, and actually would hinder productivity, because we dont have an accounts office to handle all of this. 

And given that Rusty Crewmates by this time are a team that are not unknowns, they are promoted to to trusted parties at least in Decentration eyes, and seems best suited to structure this way. We would not have done this with unknowns. However these proposals, and everyone else proposals can all be structured better, and we are dynamically refining. 

However its definitely an unchaotic situation, we have Kanban board of tasks. [https://trello.com/b/pIpbEGuZ/kabocha](https://trello.com/b/pIpbEGuZ/kabocha). It is clear what developer 1 and 2 are working on, we have a system. Sometimes tasks are shared. We have a buddy and support system.

Am I the only one getting a bit lost with the KAB delivery costs? 

Despite claims that KAB would launch very fast ("the fastest parachain launch"), there is no official launch programmed. Most of the chains that launched on Kusama did it on the week of the crowdloan settlement (which happens a couple of weeks after the end of the crowdloan period), albeit with limited functionalities. 
One could claim this is because KAB is better and will launch with every functionality already there so that it never needs to improve, but for some reason, when we see that all other teams, often conducted by pretty smart people do otherwise, it is fair to question that strategy.

I thought the role of technical steward would incorporate technical aspects such as that one above. Maybe it stems from the previous ambiguity of the proposals that we already discussed, and even if that is set to change, I hardly see how we need one runtime dev that does not provide stewardship or vice versa with the current level of advance and growth of the project. Getting a developer and a project manager is one person too much at this stage. 
To me stewardship requires mastery of runtime and pallet devs and since those are the most critical parts of the technical deliveries, I would not see why they would be outsourced. It does make little technical sense, and in the context of our current treasury spending rate, it does not make sense financially either.

Can anybody clarify the role of everyone, and the planned expenses please?
Can we also focus on mainnet launch and see how successful it is before getting engaged into further expenses.

> Am I the only one getting a bit lost with the KAB delivery costs?

I don't know but maybe you are looking for ways to be lost. 

> Despite claims that KAB would launch very fast ("the fastest parachain launch"), there is no official launch programmed. 

Yes there is here it is https://www.notion.so/kabocha-network/2547da4fcd454dcd8699499fa404ede2?v=4411177ca359405bbd73b5896e9d234e

You can also view the tasks we're working on here: https://trello.com/b/pIpbEGuZ/kabocha

> I thought the role of technical steward would incorporate technical aspects such as that one above. 

No the role of technical steward doesnt cover all aspects entirely. MY technical stewardship vision is to grow and nurture a team of collaborators. 

> I hardly see how we need one runtime dev that does not provide stewardship or vice versa with the current level of advance and growth of the project. Getting a developer and a project manager is one person too much at this stage.

I completely disagree. Without product management, developer advocacy, we will be a barren field, like i saw edgeware when i first arrived here, improverished from devs. Its probably because of points of view like this which block growth and collaboration of a team. 
If you think is easy and simple, why dont you do it? I will happily move.

> To me stewardship requires mastery of runtime and pallet devs and since those are the most critical parts of the technical deliveries, I would not see why they would be outsourced. 

Everyday i am improving and as a steward, and with grassroots development values, its to invite talent to work and develop the project. Not "outsource" as you say. 

> Can anybody clarify the role of everyone, and the planned expenses please?

If you read the proposal you will understand that we have been working with rusty crewmate initially as bounty, then as proposal for pallet, and now as fixed monthly payments. I work very well with Nathan and Timothee, and i dont see why your opinions should chang
